title: pcap_pktdata: Restore the record's pkt_encap after calling
description:
Some of the dissectors (such as Bluetooth), look at the records's
pkt_encap value so we need to update it. However, make sure to always
restore it after calling the dissector, because otherwise wiretap
will produce an error when trying to dump the packet from the check
in pcapng_write_enhanced_packet_block that the IDB's encapsulation
matches that of the packet's pkt_encap. E.g., if the frame's WTAP
encapsulation is Ethernet, and the Ethernet has IP, then UDP, then
RFTap or similar, pkt_encap needs to be restored at the end.

The fuzz sample in #21372 has a packet for which this happens, where
RFTap is used.

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
Sample file with just that packet extracted: 
[rftap-weird.pcapng](/uploads/2e723c6589d48e59f81fdf73553af64c/rftap-weird.pcapng)

That file also shows another possible enhancement - when exporting only selected packets, all the IDBs in the file are preserved instead of reducing them down to only the ones used (which would require renumbering.)
